us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic stories from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters denied White House access after Trump ban
bullets: Reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico said they were blocked from the White House on Saturday.
The denials followed President Donald Trump’s statement that he was barring the outlets over coverage he called fake news.
Press-freedom groups and the White House Correspondents’ Association criticized the move and called for access to be restored.

articles.title: High gas prices intensify voter frustration as midterm voting begins
bullets: AP reported voter frustration over sharply higher gasoline prices tied to the Iran war.
Trump called the higher prices an inexpensive price to pay for the war, a statement drawing political scrutiny.
The issue is adding pressure on Republicans as early voting gets underway for the November midterms.

articles.title: Fed rate hike renews affordability concerns across the US economy
bullets: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate on Wednesday, prompting renewed attacks from Trump.
AP reported economists see sticky inflation, stronger demand and supply shocks as key drivers of higher borrowing costs.
Affordability remains a major voter concern ahead of the midterm elections.

articles.title: US military says Caribbean boat strike killed four suspected smugglers
bullets: The US military said it struck a boat in the Caribbean on Saturday and killed four people.
Officials said the vessel was suspected of drug smuggling.
AP reported the strike is part of the Trump administration’s ongoing campaign against alleged traffickers in Latin America.

articles.title: Trump says planned Washington arch would house drones and snipers
bullets: Trump said his proposed arch near Arlington Memorial Bridge would become a military complex.
He said the site would be able to host drones, snipers and ammunition storage.
The comments expanded the security purpose of a project previously described as a monumental arch.

global.label: Global
global.subtitle: Major international developments from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: Ukraine launches massive drone attack on Russia, including Moscow
bullets: Ukraine fired more than 1,000 drones at Russia, AP reported.
Hundreds were launched toward Moscow, according to the report.
Moscow’s mayor described the strike as the largest drone attack on the Russian capital.

articles.title: North Korea fires two ballistic missiles toward the sea
bullets: South Korea’s military said North Korea launched two short-range ballistic missiles on Sunday.
The launches followed North Korean threats to strengthen its nuclear deterrent.
Japan said it detected a suspected missile but that it did not land in Japanese waters.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis attempted ballistic-missile attack on Riyadh
bullets: Saudi Arabia confirmed that Yemen’s Houthi rebels tried to attack Riyadh with a ballistic missile.
AP reported it was the first such targeting of the Saudi capital in the latest escalation.
The attempt comes as fighting with Iran-backed Houthis opens another front linked to the wider Iran war.

articles.title: Russia’s parliamentary election enters final day amid Ukraine war backdrop
bullets: Russia’s State Duma election entered its third and final day on Sunday.
Reuters reported the Kremlin casts the vote as a test of support for the war in Ukraine.
United Russia is expected to retain dominance in a political system critics say suppresses dissent.

articles.title: World leaders return to UN amid wars in Middle East and Ukraine
bullets: World leaders are gathering in New York for the UN General Assembly.
Reuters reported the agenda is dominated by the Middle East, Ukraine and AI risks.
Nearly 130 heads of state are expected as the UN faces funding, relevance and leadership pressures.

india.label: India News
india.subtitle: Top India-focused stories from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh prepares response to drought-like conditions
bullets: Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed drought-like conditions affecting Andhra Pradesh.
Officials said a preliminary assessment identified risk across 513 mandals in 28 districts.
Naidu asked district collectors to submit drought proposals by September 24.

articles.title: India says INS Kolkata was on routine deployment during Pakistan-vessel collision
bullets: India identified INS Kolkata as the warship involved in a North Arabian Sea collision with Pakistan’s PNS Hunain.
The MEA said the Pakistani vessel conducted itself in an unacceptable and unprofessional manner.
Indian officials said INS Kolkata suffered no major damage and remains at sea.

articles.title: Southwest monsoon begins retreat as India records rainfall deficit
bullets: The IMD said the southwest monsoon began withdrawing from parts of west Rajasthan.
The retreat began shortly after the normal September 17 withdrawal date.
Reports said nationwide seasonal rainfall remained below normal as the withdrawal began.

articles.title: BCCI says it pays about ₹3,000 crore in annual tax
bullets: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the board pays roughly ₹3,000 crore in income tax annually.
The disclosure was made during the BCCI’s 95th Annual General Meeting in Mumbai.
The statement came after Supreme Court questions about BCCI’s status under the National Sports Governance Act.

articles.title: India begins Asian Games campaign after Nagoya opening ceremony
bullets: The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games officially opened in Japan on Saturday.
Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat led India’s contingent at the opening ceremony.
Indian athletes are scheduled across multiple Day 2 events on September 20.

stocks.label: US Stocks
stocks.subtitle: Notable US market movers and trading themes

articles.title: Nvidia leads megacap gains in mixed session
bullets: Nvidia rose 1.34% to $222.27 in the tracked megacap group.
The stock was the strongest performer among the seven megacaps tracked by ieconomy.
The move kept AI-linked sentiment positive despite mixed megacap trading.

articles.title: Meta posts the sharpest decline among tracked megacaps
bullets: Meta fell 2.43% to $665.75 in the same megacap screen.
It was the weakest performer among Nvidia, Amazon, Alphabet, Apple, Tesla, Microsoft and Meta.
The drop weighed on the communications and megacap cohort.

articles.title: Amazon gains 1% as megacap leadership narrows
bullets: Amazon rose 1.00% to $253.71 in the tracked session.
The gain placed Amazon behind Nvidia among positive megacap movers.
The broader megacap group remained split rather than broadly higher.

articles.title: Alphabet advances while several megacaps slip
bullets: Alphabet rose 0.64% to $349.54 in the tracked megacap session.
Its gain joined Nvidia and Amazon as the positive side of the group.
Apple, Tesla, Microsoft and Meta were lower or flat in the same screen.

articles.title: Netflix drops after Wells Fargo downgrade
bullets: Netflix closed down 4.67% at $71.79 on Friday.
Wells Fargo downgraded the stock to Underweight and cut its price target to $57.
The downgrade cited weaker engagement and concerns about the company’s content slate.

articles.title: Porsche could face another 4,000 job cuts in Volkswagen turnaround plan
bullets: Reuters reported that Volkswagen’s turnaround plan may include more than 4,000 additional Porsche job cuts.
The reported cuts follow a profit warning tied to problems at Porsche.
Porsche and Volkswagen declined to comment on the Handelsblatt report.

articles.title: Anthropic weighs new AI model release ahead of expected IPO
bullets: Reuters reported Anthropic is considering releasing a new AI model.
The potential release would respond to competitive pressure from OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra.
The timing comes after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slower AI capability releases on safety grounds.

articles.title: TikTok privacy settlement hits hurdle in US court
bullets: TikTok and ByteDance’s proposed $400 million settlement with the Justice Department faced a setback.
A federal judge signaled he would reject part of the agreement, Reuters reported.
The case involves allegations that TikTok failed to protect children’s privacy and collected personal information improperly.

articles.title: Netflix downgrade puts streaming strategy under investor scrutiny
bullets: Wells Fargo cut Netflix to Underweight from Equal Weight.
Analysts cited engagement risk and a weaker second-half content slate.
Netflix shares fell sharply after the downgrade, making it a notable Friday market mover.

articles.title: US and China open talks on AI, tariffs and critical minerals
bullets: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng were set to meet in New York.
Reuters reported the talks cover AI, tariffs, rare-earth magnets and critical minerals.
The discussions are meant to prepare possible agreements before the Trump-Xi summit in Washington.

tech.label: Tech
tech.subtitle: Major technology stories from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: AI companies sued over alleged agreement to slow development
bullets: A lawsuit accuses Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google of an illegal AI slowdown agreement.
The complaint alleges coordination among competitors over AI development pace.
The companies face claims tied to antitrust law and consumer subscription value.

articles.title: China’s CXMT says new memory-chip platform has entered mass production
bullets: Chinese DRAM maker CXMT said its fifth-generation technology platform entered mass production.
Reuters reported the platform could strengthen China’s challenge to Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
CXMT said the new platform improves data capacity and production efficiency.

articles.title: Judge signals rejection of part of TikTok children’s privacy settlement
bullets: A US judge signaled concern with part of TikTok and ByteDance’s $400 million privacy settlement.
The Justice Department case alleges failures to protect children’s privacy.
The ruling signal adds uncertainty to TikTok’s attempt to resolve the case.

articles.title: Anthropic considers new model as AI rivalry intensifies
bullets: Reuters reported Anthropic is considering a new AI model rollout before an expected IPO.
The move would counter OpenAI’s momentum after the launch of GPT-6 Astra.
The report highlights tension between AI safety calls and competitive product pressure.

articles.title: Consumer AI race shifts toward personal agents
bullets: Axios reported that startups and major tech firms are racing to build persistent personal AI agents.
The products aim to act as digital proxies that know users’ preferences and routines.
OpenAI, Meta and other companies are part of the emerging consumer-agent competition.
